title: Upper-bound characterisation of public-coin communication complexity
statement: Fix a function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, a real error bound $\varepsilon$, and a natural number $m$. Then the $\varepsilon$-error one-way public-coin communication complexity of $f$ is at most $m$ (as an element of $\bbn_\infty$) if and only if there exist a length $n \in \bbn$ and a one-way public-coin protocol $p$ over the coin-tape space $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ such that $p$ $\varepsilon$-computes $f$ and the bit cost of $p$ is at most $m$.
hypotheses_covered: f : X → Y → α a function of two arguments
replaced:
For $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$, and $m \in \mathbb{N}$,
the complexity satisfies $\mathrm{CC}(f,\varepsilon) \le m$ if and only if there
exist $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a protocol $p$ over $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ such that
$p$ $\varepsilon$-computes $f$ and $p.\mathrm{cost} \le m$.
